chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said:

I, Al-Mu'alla, and Uthman ibn Imran entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When he saw us, he said: 'Welcome, welcome to you! Faces that love us and we love them. May Allah make you with us in this world and the Hereafter.' Uthman said to him: 'May I be your ransom.' He said: 'Yes, what is it?' He said: 'I am an affluent man.' He said to him: 'May Allah bless you in your affluence.'

A man comes to me and asks me for something, and it is not the time for my Zakat.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The loan with us has eighteen [rewards], and charity has ten. And what is the harm upon you if you are as you say, affluent? Give it to him. So when it becomes the time of your Zakat, count it from the Zakat. O Uthman! Do not repel him, for repelling him is great with Allah.'

O Uthman! If you knew the status of the Believer with his Lord, you would not slacken in fulfilling his need. And whoever brings joy to a Believer, he has brought it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And fulfilling the need of a Believer repels insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving money as a gift when it is not the time for Zakat, and how does it relate to Zakat rewards?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects Uthman ibn Imran’s hesitation to treat loans as charity by clarifying that the reward for lending is eighteen times greater than that of charity, and one may count the loan towards Zakat obligations even if given outside the Zakat season. The Imam underscores the spiritual magnitude of serving a believer, linking the alleviation of physical ailments like leprosy and madness to the act of fulfilling their needs, thereby elevating social welfare to a means of divine purification.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from his father, from Uqba Bin Khalid who said,

‘I and Al-Moalla, and Usman Bin Imran went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So when he<sup>asws</sup> saw us, said: ‘Welcome! Welcome with you all; faces that love us<sup>asws</sup> and we<sup>asws</sup> love them. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Cause you all to be with us<sup>asws</sup> in the world and the Hereafter’. So Usman said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Yes, what is it (that you have come for)?’ I am an affluent man’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you in your affluence’.

He said, ‘The man comes to me, so he asks me for something, and it is not the time for my Zakat?’ 
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘The loan, with us<sup>asws</sup> is with eighteen (Rewards) and the charity is with ten, and what is that upon you when you are as you are saying, ‘affluent’? Give it to him. So when it would be the time of your Zakat, count it to be from the Zakat. O Usman! Do not repel him, for the repelling is grievous in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

O Usman! You, if you were to know what is the status of the Believer from his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, you will not slacken with regards to his need; and the one who enters the joy upon a Believer, so he has entered it upon Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>; and the fulfillment of a need of the Believer repels the insanity, and the leprosy, and the vitiligo’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from his father from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“I went to visit abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Two other people, al-Mu‘alla’ and ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar, also were present with me. On seeing us, he welcomed us and offered greetings of peace, saying, ‘I welcome the faces that love us and we love them. May Allah keep you with us in this world and in the next life.’ Uthman then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ The Imam acknowledged his expression and asked, ‘What can I do for you?’ Uthman then said, ‘I am an affluent man.’ The Imam said, ‘May Allah make your wealth a blessing for you.’

He then said, ‘A man comes to me for (financial) help. Such time is not the time for me to pay zakat.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Providing a loan, before us, has eighteen rewards, and for charity it is ten rewards. You have no difficulty, being an affluent man as you just said. You can provide him help and when the time for paying zakat comes, count it as your zakat paid to him. O ‘Uthman, do not turn him away empty-handed; it is a great and serious matter in the sight of Allah.

O ‘Uthman, if you had known how important a believer is in the sight of Allah, you would not hesitate to respond positively to his appeal. Whoever provides happiness for a believing person has done so for the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. Providing help for a believing person repels illnesses like insanity, leprosy and albino (leprosy).”’
